title: WHAT IF YOU FELL FROM 10,000 METERS?
hook_text:
WHAT IF YOU FELL
FROM 10,000 METERS?
voice_style: Deep, calm male documentary narrator (ElevenLabs Adam/Brian), stability ~50%, natural pace.

segments.heading: 10,000 M · NO PARACHUTE
segments.text: You just fell out of a plane. Ten thousand meters up.

segments.heading: -50 °C · THIN AIR
segments.text: Minus fifty degrees. The air is so thin, you can barely breathe.

segments.heading: ACCELERATING
segments.text: Ten seconds in, you're past two hundred and fifty kilometers per hour.

segments.heading: TOP SPEED
segments.text: Twenty seconds. Three hundred and fourteen. Your top speed.

segments.heading: THE TWIST
segments.text: Then something strange happens. You start slowing down.

segments.heading: WHY? THICKER AIR
segments.text: The air gets thicker as you fall, and drag brakes you.

segments.heading: IMPACT IN SECONDS
segments.text: Two hundred kilometers per hour. And the ground is rushing up.

segments.heading: BUT… 1972
segments.text: Survival is almost impossible. Yet in 1972, a flight attendant fell from even higher, and lived.
segments.event: Vesna Vulović, Guinness record 10,160 m, inside fuselage section.

display: two hundred and fifty kilometers per hour
